name: Edgar Joseph
life: “I still remember painting shadow cats on my first locker.” Saturday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Edgar pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I draw the alley bins because my mother knows cities by their cats.
appearance: Edgar has black hair twisted into a small knot, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. When somebody else has the floor, Edgar turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Edgar is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Edgar asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To draw the city's working cats for family.
family: Rain Yang is Edgar’s cousin raised in the same household. Edgar leaves the first voice message. Rain calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The new language at dinner*, Rain says, “I speak his language but the agency only knows I clean offices.”
connections: Hank Fry. An onboard drawing gives the souvenir seller an alternative to the hotel view.
